title: The 10x developer is NOT a myth
summary: Brikman argues 10x developers are real: multiple studies find order-of-magnitude differences, productivity can be reasoned about without perfect metrics, and great programmers win by better decisions, though they are rare.

assertions.quote: the general finding that "There are order-of-magnitude differences among programmers" has been confirmed by many other studies of professional programmers
Just because something is hard to measure doesn’t mean we can’t reason about it.

verdicts.note: Epistemic framing rather than a testable claim.

assertions.quote: You become a 10x programmer not by doing an order of magnitude more work, but by making better decisions an order of magnitude more often.
a great programmer will know that errors are much more costly to fix later
I wouldn’t recommend building a hiring strategy around solely hiring “rock stars”; you’ll end up looking foolish and lonely.
the type of hires that can sink an organization, actively increasing tech debt with every line of code they write
